subject: RE: ACME - MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmarks, latency/cost targets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acme.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - MAP: Technical evaluation plan (benchmarks, latency/cost targets) - post-call recap

Hi Alex / Jenna - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

Summary of needs
- Primary use: customer support summarization + intent extraction across long conversation histories (~8k token context).
- Success criteria: maintain >=92% intent extraction F1 on labeled dev set; summaries acceptable to product team (qualitative checklist).
- Non-functional: sub-200ms 95th percentile generation latency for single-turn replies at 2k token context; target per-request cost <$0.015 (hosted) for production scale.

Immediate MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (owner: ACME + Redwood)
- Deliverable: benchmark harness + runbook, model shortlist, latency/cost targets, pass/fail criteria, sample data & evaluation timeline.
- Proposed timeline: draft MAP by Aug 17, benchmark runs Aug 18-24, results review Aug 26, decision by Aug 31.
- Dependencies: ACME to provide 10-20 representative conversation threads + labeling schema by Aug 17; Redwood to provide benchmark harness + baseline model runs.

Action items
1) Alex/Jenna: share sample dataset and any anonymization constraints (due Aug 17).
2) Camila / Redwood: share MAP draft and benchmark template (I'll coordinate with Camila; deliver Aug 17).
3) Schedule 45m follow-up to review results (proposed Aug 26 - options in calendar invite).

Attachments: referenced MAP template (stub) - we'll attach the editable MAP and a short PDF of latency/cost targets in follow-up.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0122

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acme.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME - MAP: Technical evaluation plan (draft)

Hi all - attaching the MAP v0.3 draft and a short PDF with the latency & cost baseline estimates we discussed. Highlights below; full details are in the attachment (ACME-MAP-v0.3.xlsx).

Technical evaluation milestone (draft) - owner / milestones / success criteria
- Owner: Camila (Redwood) + Alex (ACME)
- Milestone 1 (Data handoff) - Due: 2027-08-17 - Alex to provide 15 anonymized conversation threads + label schema.
- Milestone 2 (Benchmark harness + baseline runs) - Due: 2027-08-20 - Redwood to run 3 baseline models on ACME data and report latency/cost.
- Milestone 3 (Optimization pass) - Due: 2027-08-24 - test batching, KV caching, and 4-bit quantized variants.
- Milestone 4 (Results review + recommendation) - Due: 2027-08-26 - joint review to pick model variant for production pilot.

Benchmark success criteria (pass/fail):
- Intent extraction: F1 >= 0.92 on ACME-labeled set OR improvement of >=6% vs current baseline.
- Summarization quality: human eval acceptability >= 85% (simple 3-point rubric included).
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 200ms for single-turn generation at 2k tokens on our dedicated instance profile (p3-equivalent).
- Cost: projected per-request token cost <= $0.015 at expected QPS with suggested batching.

Model shortlist (initial)
- Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized 4-bit) - good quality/latency balance
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (optimized) - low latency, smaller memory footprint
- OpenLLaMA-3B (fine-tuned) - cost-efficient baseline

Notes on evaluation setup
- Redwood will provision a temporary dedicated pool for consistent latency measurement; results will include token-level cost breakdown and GPU utilization.
- If ACME wants, we can include a 70B-class variant as a quality ceiling (separate cost bucket).

Next steps
- Alex: confirm dataset delivery (Aug 17) and any redaction rules.
- Jenna: share internal decision criteria / stakeholders to loop into the Aug 26 review.
- Camila/Marissa: we will run the baseline and share preliminary numbers by EOD Aug 20.

Attachments: [ACME-MAP-v0.3.xlsx], [acme-latency-cost-targets.pdf]

Best,
Camila
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

From: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME - MAP: Technical evaluation plan (draft)

Thanks Marissa/Camila - this looks good. A few quick items from our side: 

1) Data: we can deliver 20 anonymized threads by EOD Aug 17 but need to strip PII; acceptable if we use the schema you sent.
2) Latency target: the product team is comfortable with 95th <= 250ms as long as 50th <= 120ms; they prioritized latency over the $0.015 cost if there is a tradeoff. Can you include a +/- sensitivity table in the benchmark output?
3) Model shortlist: we definitely want to see a 70B-class model as a quality ceiling for summaries, but we only need it for quality comparison (not production).

Also - can Redwood provide an outline of the labeling rubric for the human eval so our UX folks can review? Jenna will coordinate that.

One more ask: we like seeing per-route fallbacks and how Redwood would handle graceful degradation if the primary model is unhealthy. Please include a short section in the results review covering fallback options (e.g., lower-cost variant + cached replies).

Appreciate the quick turnaround - look forward to the baseline numbers.

- Alex
Director, Applied ML | ACME Corp
alex.smith@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acme.com>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME - MAP: Technical evaluation plan (final draft + next steps)

Great questions, Alex - thanks. Quick responses + updated plan attached (ACME-MAP-v0.3.xlsx - revised):

- Data handoff: confirm dataset & redaction approach (ACME delivers by EOD Aug 17). Camila will validate the sample format on receipt.
- Latency sensitivity: will include a sensitivity table (95th/50th/median) and run the 70B-class model as quality ceiling; we will label that variant as 'quality control' and exclude it from production cost targets.
- Human eval rubric: attached to the MAP as tab 'HumanEval-Rubric' - includes a 3-point acceptability scale and instructions for crowd/UX raters.
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: we added a short section describing per-route fallbacks, automatic model switch to quantized variant, and prefix-caching for repeated queries.

Revised timeline / responsibilities:
- Aug 17: ACME deliver sample dataset + redaction confirmation - owner: Alex
- Aug 18-20: Redwood baseline runs (Llama-2-13B-chat, Mistral-7B, OpenLLaMA-3B) - owner: Camila
- Aug 21-24: Optimization & quantized runs + 70B quality check - owner: Camila/Infra
- Aug 26: Results review + decision meeting (45m) - owner: joint
- Target close for MAP milestone: Aug 31 (goal: select production variant & pilot plan)

Please confirm dataset delivery and I'll lock the Aug 26 meeting invite.

Attachments: [ACME-MAP-v0.3.xlsx], [acme-latency-cost-targets.pdf]

Thanks,
